generalfeedback.text:
The earth turns eastwards through \(15^\circ\) every hour, so the sun reaches places to the east first. One degree of longitude is \(4\) minutes of time.

The difference in longitude is \({@ad@}^\circ\), so the time difference is \({@ad@} \times 4 = {@4*ad@}\) minutes. [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]Kampala[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]Accra[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]Mumbai[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]Lagos[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]Dakar[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]Jakarta[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]Rio de Janeiro[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]Mogadishu[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]Nairobi[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]Perth[[/if]] is [[if test="east"]]east[[else]]west[[/if]] of [[if test="is(ix=1)"]]Mombasa[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=2)"]]Nairobi[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=3)"]]Kisumu[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=4)"]]Garissa[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=5)"]]Nairobi[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=6)"]]Lodwar[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=7)"]]Mombasa[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=8)"]]Eldoret[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=9)"]]Dakar[[/if]][[if test="is(ix=10)"]]Lamu[[/if]], so its local time is [[if test="east"]]ahead[[else]]behind[[/if]]: \([[if test="is(floor(mod(tA0,1440)/60)<10)"]]0[[/if]]{@floor(mod(tA0,1440)/60)@}:[[if test="is(mod(mod(tA0,1440),60)<10)"]]0[[/if]]{@mod(mod(tA0,1440),60)@}\) [[if test="east"]]\(+\)[[else]]\(-\)[[/if]] \({@4*ad@}\) min \(= [[if test="is(floor(mod(tB,1440)/60)<10)"]]0[[/if]]{@floor(mod(tB,1440)/60)@}:[[if test="is(mod(mod(tB,1440),60)<10)"]]0[[/if]]{@mod(mod(tB,1440),60)@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Navigation: local time from longitude

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.7 (d) / Essential 2.3 (c): Find the local time at one place from the local time at another, using 4 minutes of time for each degree of longitude.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core and Essential Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: The time is right, but hours run from 0 to 23 and minutes from 0 to 59 on the 24-hour clock.

\(15^\circ\) make one hour, so \(1^\circ\) makes \(4\) minutes, not \(15\) minutes.
One degree is \(4\) minutes of time, not an hour.
